newsitem.title: INDIA: Cochin Refineries hopes for Friday start.
newsitem.headline: Cochin Refineries hopes for Friday start.

text.p: India's state-controlled crude oil refiner Cochin Refineries Ltd hopes to resume operations, which were halted earlier this week because of a water shortage, on Friday, a company spokesman said.
"We hope to resume operations by Friday evening," company spokesman Sajeev Nair told Reuters by telephone on Thursday from Cochin city in the southern state of Kerala.

Production at the 150,000 barrels-per-day refinery, located on the southwest coast of India, ground to a halt on Monday when water supply dwindled to 8,450 kilolitres per day compared to the refinery's daily demand of 22,750.
The refinery supplies petrol, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and diesel to the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
On Wednesday, state Irrigation Department officials said low electricity voltage and leaks in supply pipes, responsible for the sharp drop in water supply, had been fixed.
Nair said on Thursday that senior district officials had met authorities from the state's water supply and electricity departments to solve the problem.
"The electricity board assured the water department of uninterrupted power supply for the next five days and the water supply officials promised they will pump out water at full capacity," Nair said.
The daily water supply to the refinery increased to nearly 20,000 kilolitres on Wednesday, Nair said.
He said the immediate goal was to stock 60,000 kilolitres, three days' stock, before it could resume operations.
He said the state government was losing nearly 30 million rupees ($838,000) a day due to the shutdown.
Nair said it would take the refinery nearly one week after reopening to reach peak capacity. The refinery's annual production capacity is 7.5 million tonnes.
He said the refinery's crude shipments had not been affected but a backlog of crude shipments could mount if the problem persisted.
